title: The Mediterranean 32
alt: AI-created motor yacht concept; fictional asset, not an actual asset for sale
overview: A fictional motor yacht presentation built around life on deck, accommodation and the vessel’s technical record. The dimensions and operating figures demonstrate the listing format; they are not specifications for the concept image.
highlights: Accommodation and deck layout at a glance
Build, refit and maintenance history kept distinct
Tax, flag and survey position alongside the asking price
records: Title, ownership and authority to market
Builder specification, general arrangement and inventory
Engine logs and maintenance / refit records
Independent survey, class and statutory certificates
Flag, registration and VAT / customs evidence
considerations: A real yacht listing would disclose the build and refit dates, verified dimensions, flag, class, survey findings, maintenance status and any private or commercial use restrictions. Berth, crew, fuel and running costs are separate. The example price establishes no VAT-paid status.

title: The executive cabin
alt: AI-created private aircraft concept; fictional asset, not an actual asset for sale
overview: A fictional business-jet presentation that puts cabin configuration, utilisation and maintenance evidence before lifestyle claims. All figures are sample data and do not describe a real airframe or the aircraft shown.
highlights: Cabin configuration and utilisation shown first
Airframe hours and cycles presented separately
Inspection, engine and APU records inform the brief
records: Title, liens and seller authority
Airframe, engine and APU logs with dated hours / cycles

Programme enrolment and transfer conditions
Damage history, modifications and airworthiness records
considerations: A real aircraft presentation would identify the manufacturer, model, serial and registration where authorised, dated utilisation, inspections, equipment and damage history. title: The contemporary GT
alt: AI-created exotic car concept; fictional asset, not an actual asset for sale
overview: A fictional contemporary grand tourer concept. A real listing would connect specification and photographic detail with recorded mileage, service evidence and a clear ownership history.
highlights: Mileage unit stated explicitly
Factory equipment separated from later modifications
Condition, history and market specification easy to find
records: VIN and seller authority, shared appropriately
Registration, title and finance checks
Service book and supporting invoices
Condition inspection and damage disclosures
Factory specification, modifications and supplied items
considerations: A real vehicle listing would identify make, model, VIN where appropriate, recorded distance with its unit and basis, specification, service history, damage disclosures, warranty terms if any, and registration status. Import eligibility and taxes must be checked for the destination; no warranty or VAT status is implied.

title: The heritage grand tourer
alt: AI-created classic car concept; fictional asset, not an actual asset for sale
overview: A fictional classic grand tourer concept. The presentation balances design and character with the provenance, condition and restoration evidence a collector needs to examine.
highlights: Odometer reading distinguished from verified lifetime mileage
Restoration and originality claims require records
Condition and provenance lead; future value is not promised
records: Chassis, engine and body identification where appropriate
Ownership chronology and provenance file
Restoration invoices and dated photographs
Condition report including underside and corrosion
Registration, export and destination import documents
considerations: A real classic-car listing would distinguish original, restored, replaced and modified components and disclose known corrosion or structural repairs. Matching-numbers and certification claims require evidence. An odometer reading alone does not establish lifetime mileage, and no appreciation is promised.
